, reinforcing the importance of continued statin therapy during fasting
Dyslipidemia
, including practical scheduling of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), warfarin monitoring considerations, and adherence counseling
Anticoagulation
, with pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic considerations for time-dependent and concentration-dependent agents
Antibiotic therapy

“Ramadan pharmacotherapy requires more than shifting medication timing,” Dr. El Ouweini emphasized during the session. “It demands structured risk assessment, individualized therapeutic planning, close monitoring, and proactive patient education to ensure safety without compromising clinical outcomes.”

The interactive session was met with strong engagement from participants across the EMRO region, highlighting the growing interest among emerging pharmacists in culturally competent, patient-centered care.

Dr. Youness Zidoun, Director of the Simulation Center, was recently invited to speak at the prestigious 7th Zhujiang Development Forum on Simulation in Healthcare, held in Guangzhou, China. The forum brought together leaders, educators, and innovators from across Asia and beyond to advance dialogue and share best practices in clinical simulation.
Dr. Zidoun delivered two keynote sessions during the event. His first, presented at the Forum of Directors, was titled:
“Designing Excellence: The Strategic Development of Clinical Simulation Centers.”
In this session, he outlined strategic frameworks for developing high-impact simulation centers, emphasizing leadership models, infrastructure planning, and long-term sustainability.
His second keynote, delivered during the Plenary Session, was entitled:
“The AI Paradox in Healthcare: Understanding the Lag in Medical Education.”

His presentation examined the growing divide between the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence and the pace of curricular integration in health professions education. Dr. Zidoun offered insights into responsible implementation and the need for urgent upskilling of academic faculty.
“It was a privilege to contribute to such a forward-thinking forum,” Dr. Zidoun noted. “The energy, commitment, and vision emerging from China’s healthcare simulation community is truly inspiring.”
The participation highlights our institution’s growing global engagement and leadership in the field of health simulation and medical education innovation.

Professor Norcini emphasized that the most effective approach is the establishment of a holistic assessment system, ensuring coherence across courses and academic years and avoiding gaps in competency assessment.
Assessment

The conference plenary sessions delivered powerful messages to educators from the MENA region, highlighting that the primary mission of health professions education is to improve patient outcomes. To achieve this goal, universities must actively engage stakeholders and industry partners in educational design and delivery, integrate community engagement and interprofessional learning activities into curricula, and contribute to creating supportive workplace environments for healthcare professionals.

Extensive discussions addressed the role of artificial intelligence in education and clinical practice, particularly its potential to support professors and physicians in their professional tasks. However, educational psychologist Professor Janet Grant cautioned policymakers about the potential deskilling effects of AI. She advocated for its cautious and justified use by both faculty and students to ensure the development of robust cognitive skills and clinical reasoning. Ultimately, health professionals must possess sufficient subject-matter expertise to critically evaluate information and identify AI-generated inaccuracies or hallucinations.

Dr. Arina sincerely thanks the Dubai Medical University leadership for their support and encouragement to participate in international educational conferences, enabling continuous learning and the sharing of the University’s experience on a global platform.

Dubai Medical University Launches Longitudinal Interprofessional Prescribing Skills Training Program

Dubai Medical University (DMU) proudly announces the launch of a comprehensive longitudinal training program in Prescribing Skills Assessment (PSA), developed collaboratively by the College of Pharmacy and the College of Medicine. This pioneering initiative reflects the University’s commitment to advancing patient safety, interprofessional education, and practice-readiness among near-to-graduate healthcare students. The Prescribing Skills Assessment is

Dubai Medical University (DMU) proudly announces the launch of a comprehensive longitudinal training program in Prescribing Skills Assessment (PSA), developed collaboratively by the College of Pharmacy and the College of Medicine. This pioneering initiative reflects the University’s commitment to advancing patient safety, interprofessional education, and practice-readiness among near-to-graduate healthcare students.

The Prescribing Skills Assessment is designed to rigorously evaluate and strengthen students’ competencies in safe and effective prescribing. The assessment framework encompasses multiple critical domains, including:
Safe and rational prescribing
Prescription review and validation
Identification and management of adverse drug reactions
Therapeutic planning and clinical management
Laboratory and diagnostic data interpretation
Pharmaceutical calculations
Therapeutic drug monitoring
Patient communication and counseling

The program is structured as a longitudinal curriculum model beginning in Year 2 and continuing through Year 5. It progressively builds prescribing competence from foundational principles to advanced clinical application during experiential and clinical training. The initiative is fully integrated across courses within the curriculum, ensuring continuous reinforcement of prescribing competencies in both theoretical and clinical contexts.

This collaboration is particularly timely. While medical graduates are already licensed prescribers, pharmacy prescribing authority is anticipated to be introduced in the United Arab Emirates soon for selected minor ailments. By proactively preparing pharmacy graduates for this expanded scope of practice, DMU is positioning its students at the forefront of evolving healthcare delivery models in the region.

The integration is led by the College of Pharmacy under the supervision of Dr. Riza Assadi and Dr. Ahmad El-Ouweini, in close collaboration with the College of Medicine, represented by Prof. Nevien Hendawy and Dr. Rania Shalaby. This intercollege leadership exemplifies DMU’s commitment to interprofessional education (IPE) and collaborative practice.

The inaugural session of the program focused on pharmaceutical calculations, an essential foundation for safe prescribing. Students from both the College of Medicine and the College of Pharmacy participated in an interprofessional training workshop, working collaboratively in mixed groups to solve clinically oriented calculation cases. The session emphasized teamwork, shared clinical reasoning, and mutual understanding of professional roles in medication safety.

This initiative marks a significant milestone in curriculum innovation at Dubai Medical University. By embedding prescribing skills training longitudinally and interprofessionally, DMU ensures that its graduates are equipped not only with knowledge, but with the practical competence, clinical judgment, and collaborative mindset required for safe prescribing practice. The University looks forward to expanding the application of this program across additional courses and clinical experiences, further strengthening prescribing readiness and advancing excellence in healthcare education.

DMU MPharm Graduate Releases Research in Q2 Scopus-Indexed Journal

DUBAI (March 11, 2026) – Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy announces the publication of a research article authored by Ms. Zainab Almardod, a recent graduate of the Master of Pharmacy (Clinical Pharmacy Specialization) program, in the Q2, Scopus-indexed journal Critical Care Research and Practice. The article, titled “Prevalence, Risk Factors, Characteristics, and Clinical

DUBAI (March 11, 2026) – Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy announces the publication of a research article authored by Ms. Zainab Almardod, a recent graduate of the Master of Pharmacy (Clinical Pharmacy Specialization) program, in the Q2, Scopus-indexed journal
Critical Care Research and Practice
, was conducted under the supervision of Prof. Kishore Gnana Sam, a Professor of Pharmacy Practice at the college.
“Prevalence, Risk Factors, Characteristics, and Clinical Outcomes of Thrombocytopenia in the Intensive Care Unit: A Prospective Single-Center Cohort Study”

This prospective cohort study enrolled 276 critically ill patients in a tertiary intensive care unit and investigated the epidemiology and clinical impact of thrombocytopenia. The study reported a prevalence of 38.8% and an incidence of new-onset thrombocytopenia of 22.5%. Importantly, new-onset thrombocytopenia was found to be independently associated with major bleeding and increased ICU mortality. The research also identified key predictors, including shock, sepsis, and renal impairment, and highlighted medication-related factors associated with severe thrombocytopenia.

The study contributes valuable epidemiological data from the Gulf region, where ICU-related thrombocytopenia has been underrepresented in the literature. Its findings provide clinically relevant insights that may support improved risk stratification, monitoring, and management strategies in critical care settings.

This publication reflects the strong research component embedded within the MPharm (Clinical Pharmacy Specialization) program, which emphasizes methodological rigor, advanced statistical analysis, and clinically meaningful outcomes. It also demonstrates the college’s commitment to cultivating postgraduate students capable of producing high-quality, practice-oriented research that contributes to evidence-based patient care.

Professor Mirza R. Baig, Program Director for the Master of Clinical Pharmacy and Professor of Pharmacy Practice at the College of Pharmacy – Dubai Medical University (DMU), was invited as a speaker at an international conference organized by Indira University, Pune, India, held on 13–14 January 2026. During the conference, he delivered an insightful and forward-looking presentation on “Simulation Safety in Pharmacy Education: Enhancing the Role of the Clinical Pharmacist in the Patient Care Process.” His talk highlighted the critical importance of simulation-based education in preparing pharmacy graduates for safe, effective, and patient-centered clinical practice.

In addition to his keynote participation at the conference, Professor Baig was also invited to speak at several prestigious pharmacy institutions in Pune, including Modern College of Pharmacy, Bharati Vidyapeeth University, and Poona College of Pharmacy. These academic interactions provided an excellent platform for knowledge exchange and academic collaboration between institutions in India and the United Arab Emirates.

During his lectures, Professor Baig showcased how Dubai Medical University stands at the forefront of innovation in health professions education by integrating advanced simulation technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and virtual reality (VR) into its pharmacy curriculum. He emphasized that DMU adopts a learner-centered, competency-based educational model, where students are trained extensively in high-fidelity simulated environments that closely replicate real clinical settings.

This progressive approach ensures that DMU pharmacy students develop strong clinical decision-making, communication, and patient safety skills before being deployed to professional experiential training sites. By allowing students to practice and refine their competencies in a controlled, risk-free environment, DMU significantly enhances patient safety while producing practice-ready clinical pharmacists.

Professor Baig’s presentations strongly reflected DMU’s commitment to academic excellence, innovation, and global best practices in pharmacy education, reinforcing the university’s reputation as a regional and international leader in simulation-based healthcare training.

Dubai Medical University (DMU) – College of Pharmacy highlights the international academic engagement of Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice and Critical Care Clinical Pharmacist, who was recently invited as a panelist at the Residency Showcase & Career Strategy event organized by the Lebanese American University (LAU) School of Pharmacy.

The event, held at LAU, brought together PharmD students, residents, alumni, and faculty to discuss the evolving landscape of pharmacy residency training and its impact on career development. Dr. El Ouweini participated in the Alumni Panel, moderated by Dr. Mira El Masri, where he shared insights from his professional journey and highlighted the importance of advanced pharmacy training.

Drawing on his diverse experience across Lebanon and the UAE, Dr. El Ouweini reflected on his path from BPharm training in Syria, to completing his PharmD at LAU, a PGY-1 residency, and later a post-doctoral fellowship in clinical pharmacy research. Today, as a faculty member at DMU, he continues to advance clinical pharmacy education while establishing and expanding critical care services at DMU Hospital.

During the panel discussion, he emphasized how residency training shaped his clinical reasoning, teaching approach, and research capabilities. He also explained how Lebanon’s PGY-1 programs—designed in alignment with U.S. residency standards—equipped him with the competencies needed to practice confidently in international healthcare environments.
He noted that while the field has evolved from BPharm → PharmD → PGY-1, residency remains a “true investment” that enhances a pharmacist’s readiness for both local and global practice.

He encouraged students to embrace opportunities with clarity and ambition, reminding them that residency training builds not only clinical expertise but also leadership, communication, resilience, and teamwork.

Panelist in SimTalks: the Promise and Limits of VR, AR, and AI in Healthcare Simulation

As part of Simulation Week 2025 and the celebration of Simulation Champions, Dr. Sarah Sanad, Assistant Professor at the College of Nursing, participated as a panelist at the SIMTalks session, “Beyond the Bedside: The Promise and Limits of VR, AR, and AI in Simulation.” The event brought together simulation experts from the region and internationally,

As part of Simulation Week 2025 and the celebration of Simulation Champions, Dr. Sarah Sanad, Assistant Professor at the College of Nursing, participated as a panelist at the SIMTalks session, “Beyond the Bedside: The Promise and Limits of VR, AR, and AI in Simulation.” The event brought together simulation experts from the region and internationally, alongside educators, healthcare professionals, and students, to explore the evolving role of technology in clinical education.

Dr. Sanad emphasized the importance of balancing technological innovation with human-centered care, noting that empathy, intuition, and professional judgment remain essential in training future clinicians. She highlighted the need for equitable access, demonstrating that meaningful learning can be achieved through low-fidelity models, creative approaches, and collaborative partnerships, even in the absence of high-cost VR/AR/AI equipment.

Looking ahead to 2035, Dr. Sanad predicted that students will increasingly engage with AI-driven virtual environments, but she stressed that these tools must complement, not replace, real-world bedside experiences. She offered actionable recommendations for educators, including aligning technology with learning outcomes, empowering faculty to adapt tools, promoting creativity and equity, and keeping patient safety, resilience, and humanity at the core of simulation-based education.

The session highlighted both the promise and limitations of immersive technologies, reaffirming the value of blended learning models that combine virtual simulation with bedside practice to prepare competent, empathetic, and resilient healthcare professionals.

Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy has successfully concluded the Prescribing Skills Assessment (PSA) Training Series for its Pharmacy Practice faculty members.

Conducted from February to April 2025, the series forms part of the College’s ongoing professional development initiatives aimed at enhancing the proficiency in clinical pharmacy education and assessment.
This training series was launched as part of embedding the PSA into the pharmacy curriculum, with the goal of strengthening student competencies in safe and effective prescribing practices.
Faculty members engaged in a series of interactive, case-based, and hands-on sessions covering the eight core domains of the PSA:
1. Prescribing
2. Prescription Review
3. Planning Management
4. Providing Information
5. Calculation Skills
6. Adverse Drug Reactions
7. Drug Monitoring
8. Data Interpretation
These domains represent critical competencies aligned with the international Prescribing Safety Assessment framework and are vital for preparing pharmacy students for real-world clinical practice.

The College extends its sincere appreciation to all faculty members for their active participation and valuable contributions to the success of this initiative. Special thanks to Dr. Rizah Anwar Assadi, PharmD, BCPS , who led and facilitated the implementation of PSA at DMU and played a key role in supporting its integration into the academic framework.

On Wednesday, April 23, 2025, the IVPN Student Club at Dubai Medical University (DMU) hosted an inspiring international webinar in collaboration with the University of Nottingham, titled "Astropharmacy: The Science and Practice of Medication in Spaceflight." The event featured two speakers — Phil Williams Associate Pro-Vice-Chancellor, and Li Shean Toh , Assistant Professor — who shared fascinating insights into the unique challenges of providing pharmaceutical care during space missions.

The webinar sparked lively interest among pharmacy students from various universities, who tuned in to learn about how medications behave in zero gravity, how astronauts receive care during long-term missions, and the future role of pharmacists in space exploration. Beyond the science, the session encouraged students to think creatively and globally about their profession.

Bringing together academic expertise and student curiosity, this event is a testament to DMU’s dedication to delivering forward-thinking pharmacy education and building meaningful international partnerships that enrich the student learning experience.

Building on the success of the event, DMU students are now collaborating with Dr. Phil Williams and his team at the University of Nottingham to initiate a new research project focused on advancing the field of astropharmacy. This exciting development reflects DMU’s dedication to nurturing research opportunities, global collaboration, and innovation in pharmacy education.

The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University recently welcomed Dr. Osama Tabbara, President of the IVPN-Network, for an engaging and motivational workshop titled “The Skills & Qualities of Impressive Pharmacists: Raise your Self Awareness.”

The session, attended by both faculty members and pharmacy students, focused on the evolving landscape of pharmacy practice and the critical role of transformational leadership, adaptability, and professionalism in driving the profession forward.

Drawing on his extensive experience as a consultant and pharmacy leader, Dr. Tabbara inspired participants to embrace a mindset of continuous improvement and innovation. He highlighted the challenges facing the modern pharmacist — from increased competition and complex clinical responsibilities to the need for agility in a rapidly changing healthcare environment.

Through his “12 Impressive Habits” framework, Dr. Tabbara guided attendees on key personal and professional traits essential for career growth. These habits included punctuality, communication skills, visibility, engagement, adaptability, emotional intelligence, and time management, among others. Each habit was accompanied by practical self-assessment tools, encouraging participants to reflect on their own professional development.

Dr. Tabbara also emphasized the importance of mentorship, self-awareness, and teamwork, urging students to “become brands of excellence” within the pharmacy profession. His closing message, “Don’t ask when I can be promoted — ask how I can be great and impressive,” resonated strongly with the audience.

The article, titled “Cubosomes as smart nanocarriers for antimicrobial agents: A review of emerging applications,”
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a review article by faculty members and undergraduate pharmacy students in
, an internationally recognized peer-reviewed journal at the forefront of translational medicine and biomaterials science.

“Cubosomes as smart nanocarriers for antimicrobial agents: A review of emerging applications,”
Raneem Zakaria
Nour Hijazi

The review explores cubosomes — an innovative class of lipid-based nanoparticles — and their promising role in delivering antimicrobial agents. Unlike conventional drug carriers, cubosomes possess a highly ordered internal structure that allows them to efficiently encapsulate a wide range of drug types while providing sustained and controlled release. The article highlights the potential of these advanced nanocarriers to enhance the solubility and bioavailability of antibacterial, antiviral, and antifungal drugs, and to overcome major challenges such as antimicrobial resistance, rapid drug degradation, and poor drug permeability. The review also discusses their ability to disrupt biofilms and improve targeted drug delivery, alongside current limitations in large-scale manufacturing and storage stability that must be addressed before clinical translation.

He completed a postdoctoral fellowship in clinical pharmacy research with a focus on critical care—a joint program between Gulf Medical University and Washington State University. He is also a Board-Certified Pharmacotherapy Specialist (BCPS), completed ASHP-accredited PGY-1 Pharmacy Practice Residency, a certified clinical preceptor, and a licensed clinical pharmacist with credentials from the UAE, Lebanon, and the USA.

Prior to joining DMU, Dr. El Ouweini served as Clinical Lecturer and Critical Care Clinical Pharmacist at Gulf Medical University and Thumbay University Hospital between 2021-2025, and this was preceded by serving as a Clinical Lecturer and Clinical Pharmacist at Lebanese American University Medical Center between 2020-2021. His expertise spans critical care pharmacotherapy, cardiology, infectious diseases, and nephrology, and he has delivered over 50 invited presentations and workshops across international conferences. Dr. El Ouweini has authored multiple peer-reviewed publications in the field of pharmacy practice and critical care.

Beyond his academic and clinical achievements, Dr. El Ouweini plays a leading role in the IVPN-Network, where he serves as Chair of the IVPN-Webinars Organizing Committee and Leader of the IVPN-Critical Care Listserv—advancing global collaboration and continuous professional development among pharmacists. He is an active member in several international pharmacy organizations, including ACCP, ASHP, and the European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM), where he serves as the Social Media and Digital Lead for the Pharmacology and Pharmacotherapy Section. The College of Pharmacy is excited to have Dr. El Ouweini on board and looks forward to his contributions in advancing clinical education, interdisciplinary practice, and research excellence at DMU.

Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr. Bassam Atallah, Pharm.D., M.S., BCPS, FHFSA, FCCP, as Associate Dean for Clinical Affairs, College of Pharmacy. Dr. Atallah brings with him a portfolio of academic, clinical, research, and leadership experience that has advanced pharmacy education and practice in the UAE and the region for over a decade.

Dr. Atallah has most recently served as a Senior Pharmacotherapy Specialist at Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi and Clinical Associate Professor at Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine where he contributed to some “Clinical firsts” in the UAE including the development of innovative pharmacist-led clinics. Prior to moving to the UAE, he served in the faculty of Clinical Pharmacy at King Saud bin Abdulaziz University for Health Sciences (KSAU-HS) in Riyadh. He has also served different roles as subject matter expert with the Department of Health Abu Dhabi and Ministry of Education Commission for Academic Accreditation. In addition to his contributions to many other academic institutions in the UAE and beyond, thus bringing a wealth of international, regional and local academic experience.

Dr Atallah received his PharmD from Bernard J. Dunn School of Pharmacy in Virginia and completed an ASHP accredited post graduate residency at Winchester Medical Center in Virginia, USA. He was awarded the “Graduate of the Last Decade” award by his alma mater. Dr Atallah is a fellow of the Heart Failure Society of America (HFSA) and the American College of Clinical Pharmacy (ACCP). He has many publications and presentations at national and international conferences. He was awarded the 2021 ACCP Cardiology PRN international award. His research interests are in various aspects of cardiovascular pharmacotherapy with a focus on antithrombotic therapy, heart failure and hyperlipidemia. At Dubai Medical University, Dr. Atallah is expected to lead the experiential clinical education components of the PharmD and Master’s programs. This is in addition to contributing to curriculum development, didactic education and clinical faculty development. In addition to his academic responsibilities, Dr. Atallah will lead the development of pharmacy clinical services at affiliated sites including at Dubai Medical University Hospital. His appointment will set the stage for future development of postgraduate training programs in clinical pharmacy at affiliated sites. With a strong track record of practice, teaching and research, Dr. Atallah appointment marks a significant step toward strengthening Dubai Medical University’s academic and clinical excellence and innovation in contemporary pharmacy education.

Dubai Medical University is the first specialized educational institution in medicine and pharmacy in the United Arab Emirates, with over 40 years of experience in higher education. It was launched with a solid vision to invest in women’s education, empower them, and enhance their role in healthcare and medical sciences.

Since its founding, the university has been committed to providing high-quality academic programs with international accreditation and agreements with prestigious international universities, with a focus on academic excellence, practical training, and integrated healthcare, within an advanced educational environment that supports female students and provides them with opportunities for excellence and innovation.

Today, the university includes leading colleges in the fields of medicine, pharmacy, and nursing. The newly accredited nursing program is a strategic step in line with the UAE’s National Agenda, which aims to increase the number of qualified healthcare professionals to meet the growing needs of the healthcare sector and enhance the quality and sustainability of healthcare services.

The university boasts modern educational programs and teaching plans that align with global requirements, advanced laboratories and technologies focused on artificial intelligence and virtual reality labs, and a highly qualified and experienced faculty, making it a preferred academic destination for ambitious female students seeking excellence in healthcare.

The university offers 100% full scholarships to UAE nationals in the Pharmacy and Nursing programs, as part of its cooperation with the NAFES program, to support the development of national cadres in the healthcare sector.

The university also offers scholarships of up to 40%, enhancing access to high-quality medical education for all female students, at prices considered among the lowest in the country despite the advanced level of education.

To learn more about the programs and specializations, the university invites interested female students and their parents to visit the university’s headquarters in Dubai – Muhaisnah 1, from Monday to Friday, from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, to meet with faculty members and visit the university’s laboratories and facilities.

Dubai students to get unprecedented access to top Indian universities like AIIMS, IIMA

A deal

Students in Dubai will soon have access to top Indian universities like All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Indian Institute of Management (IIM) and Indian Institute of Foreign Trade (IIFT), thanks to agreements signed during the first India visit of Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai.

A deal was signed between Dubai Medical University (DMU) and the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) — one of the South Asian country’s top medical institutes — which gives students from DMU an opportunity to have an exchange programme in India.

The cooperation agreement, signed by Yahya Saeed Lootah, Vice Chairman of the Board of DMU, and Ahamadulla Shariff, Head of the Department of Anatomy at AIIMS, aims to strengthen academic and research collaboration.

According to Dr Shariff, the program will begin this year. “Initially, there will be some posting of DMCG students for a short time as observers, along with our students, at AIMS Delhi,” he told Khaleej Times. “Based on the requirement, some of our professors may come over for a short time as visiting faculty.”

Sheikh Hamdan’s two-day visit to the country, which came at the invite of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi saw several landmark agreements being signed, strengthening cooperation between both countries significantly.

“This is a great opportunity for our students,” said Denis Lefrancois, advisor to the chairman of S.S. Lootah group. “With the history of the AIIMS, all of their great experience, skills, facilities that they have, the number of patients that they see, the number of students that go through the institution, it is so going to be a great experience for our students.”

The AIIMS is a group of public medical universities in India. The oldest one was established in 1956 in New Delhi and currently there are 20 operational universities, with at least three more expected in the coming years. Considered one of the finest medical universities in India, AIIMS collectively takes in over 2,000 students every year.

Key areas of collaboration include joint research in priority fields such as infectious diseases, metabolic disorders, and climate change, and the development of global health initiatives. The agreement also provides a framework for the exchange of academic materials and research publications. The agreement also covers cooperation with AIIMS in areas related to AI research, development, and digital transformation in medical education and healthcare.

Biography

Dr. Abdullah joined Dubai Medical College for Girls in 2023 as a full-time assistant professor in the nursing program. Dr. Abdullah worked in several hospital areas as a registered nurse, gaining clinical experience in emergency departments, intensive care, geriatric, psychology, home health, school health, and outpatient mental health. Dr. Khaled Elmasry, MD, MSc, PhD, is an Assistant Professor of Human Anatomy and Embryology in the Department of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine, Dubai Medical University, Dubai, UAE. He graduated with an MBBS (MD) with Honors from the Faculty of Medicine, Mansoura University, Egypt (2007) and completed an MSc in Basic Medical Sciences (Human Anatomy and Embryology) at the same university (2011). Dr. Elmasry earned his PhD in Biomedical Sciences (Cellular Biology and Anatomy) from the Medical College of Georgia at Augusta University, USA (2018). His postgraduate training includes postdoctoral fellowships at Schepens Eye Research Institute, Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA (2018-2019) and at Oakland University’s Eye Research Institute, Rochester, MI, USA (2021–2022).

Dr. Elmasry previously served as an Assistant Professor of Human Anatomy and Embryology at Mansoura Faculty of Medicine, Mansoura University, Mansoura, Egypt (2019–2024) and later at the Dental College of Georgia, Augusta University (2022–2025), where he directed courses in craniofacial and gastrointestinal anatomy and led Bio clinical seminars. His research focuses on extracellular vesicle signaling, hypoxia and inflammation in diabetic retinopathy, bone morphogenetic proteins, retinal neurovascular physiology, and the therapeutic effects of natural compounds. He has authored numerous peer‑reviewed articles and received multiple awards, including the Vision Discovery Institute award of excellence in vision research and the 2018 People’s Choice Prize in the Three‑Minute Thesis competition. He was also awarded the New Faculty Teaching Excellence Award from the Dental College of Georgia (2024). Dr. Elmasry is an active member of professional societies, such as the Egyptian Medical Syndicate and the Association for Research in Vision and Ophthalmology.

Prof. Naglaa Gamil Shehab is a Professor in the Pharmaceutical Sciences Department at Dubai Pharmacy College for Girls, UAE, and a Professor in the Pharmacognosy Department at the Faculty of Pharmacy, Cairo University, Egypt. She earned her Bachelor’s degree in Pharmaceutical Sciences in 1991, her Master’s in Pharmacognosy in 1999, and her PhD in 2004, all from Cairo University. Prof. Naglaa was promoted to Professor at Dubai Pharmacy College for Girls in 2015 and at Cairo University in 2018. With over 30 years of teaching experience, she has held various leadership positions in both institutions, including Head of the Admission Committee, Student Affairs, Curriculum Development, Faculty Development, and Research Unit. She also served as Chief Academic Officer at Dubai Pharmacy College for Girls and finally as Associate Dean of Academic Affairs, at Dubai Pharmacy College for Girls.

Prof. Naglaa is a member of the American Society of Pharmacognosy and holds certifications in nutrition and health. She introduced a pioneering course on “Natural Medicines, Safety, and Efficacy” at Dubai Pharmacy College, which focuses on drug-herb interactions and supplement quality control, a first of its kind in the Arab region. Her role as Associate Dean of Academic Affairs has provided her with extensive experience in community, industrial, and hospital training, enabling her to collaborate effectively with training heads at Dubai Pharmacy College.

Prof. Naglaa has received prestigious research awards from Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Amsterdam in the field of Natural Products. She has been recognized among the top two thousand scientists in the UAE. As a reviewer for numerous international journals in natural products, she has published over 40 scientific papers in impact factor journals. To continuously advance her career, she regularly participates in workshops, seminars, webinars, and conferences in the field of education.

Dr. Rana Sammour is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences and Associate Dean for Academic Affairs at Dubai Medical University. She holds a Bachelor of Pharmacy with Honors, two master’s degrees in Pharmaceutical Technology and Health Administration, and a PhD in Pharmaceutical Technology.

Her academic expertise includes pharmaceutics, biopharmaceutics, pharmaceutical technology, novel drug delivery systems, and pharmacy education. Her research focuses on advanced drug delivery systems, including proniosomes, nanocarriers, microsponges, buccal films, in situ gels, and strategies to improve drug solubility, stability, and bioavailability.

Dr. Sammour has published several peer-reviewed research articles and supervised student research projects in pharmaceutical formulation, and drug delivery. She is also actively involved in academic leadership, curriculum development, student affairs, academic advising, and institutional committees.

Her current interests include integrating artificial intelligence and emerging technologies into pharmaceutical sciences, drug delivery research, and higher education to support innovation and future-ready pharmacy graduates.

Dr. Rania Hamed Shalaby is an Egyptian pharmacologist, medical educator, and academic leader with over 18 years of distinguished service. She obtained her M.B.B.Ch. (2005), M.Sc. (2011), and Ph.D. (2016) in Basic Medical Sciences (Pharmacology) from Tanta University, Egypt, where she also serves as an Assistant Professor.

She joined the College of Medicine (COM) in 2016 as an Assistant Professor of Pharmacology and currently serves as an Associate Professor of Pharmacology at Dubai Medical College for Girls (DMCG) since 2023. In 2025, she was appointed Director of the Student Success Centre (SSC) at COM.

A 2024 JMHPE graduate (Maastricht–Suez Canal University), Dr. Shalaby is a regional leader in portfolio-based assessment and mentorship programs. She coordinates the Renal, Cardiovascular System (CVS) & pharmacology courses, supervises Master of Addiction Sciences theses, and leads innovative PBL development projects across COM.

Her research focuses on pharmacological interventions addressing inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolic disorders, with several peer-reviewed publications indexed in Scopus and Web of Science. As SSC Director, she oversees student appeals and grievances, academic advising, attendance monitoring, and peer tutoring programs, ensuring holistic academic guidance and support for student success.

Dr. Rawan Ahmed Mehanna is a Clinical Teaching Assistant in the Department of Clinical Sciences at Dubai Medical University College of Medicine. A graduate of Dubai Medical College for Girls, she earned her MBBCh degree in 2021 and has since dedicated herself to advancing clinical education with a focus on innovation, empathy, and experiential learning. In 2024, shecompleted the Advance HE ( UK ), Certification in Learning and Teaching in Higher Education, further strengthening her expertise in medical education.

She is also a certified NIHS OSCE Case Designer ( Al Ain, 2024 ), enhancing her contribution to assessment and evaluation. Dr. Mehanna is an active member of the DMU Simulation Center team as a simulation educator and certified BLS Instructor, where she contributes to the design and facilitation of simulation sessions, skill-based learning experiences and essential BLS training. With a passion for simulation-based education and gamification, she strives to bridge theory with practice, empowering medical students to think critically and perform confidently in real clinical settings.

Known for her commitment to academic excellence and her student-centered approach, Dr. Mehanna continues to explore ways to enhance teaching methodologies and strategies. Her professional interests include neurology and neuroscience, alongside medical education research, with a continuous drive to inspire future clinicians through innovative learning.

Beyond academia, Dr. Mehanna is a passionate volunteer, with certified training from SANID and DCAS. She actively participates in community outreach and medical services volunteering at major sports championships. She believes in giving back to the community and inspiring her students to embrace compassion and service as integral parts of the medical profession

Dr. Shifan Khanday is a physician, anatomist, and academic leader specializing in the integration of artificial intelligence within medical education.She holds dual doctorates—a Ph.D. from St George’s and Kingston University of London (UK) and a Doctorate in Anatomy from Sri Ramachandra Medical University —A Diplomate in Family Medicine with Royal College of Physicians ,London ,United Kingdom she also holds Master’s degrees in Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare ( Spain) and a Master’s in Health Professions Education (Maastricht University, Netherlands). A qualified Family Medicine physician with an MBA in Healthcare leadership she combines clinical insight with advanced expertise in digital transformation and higher-education innovation.

At Dubai Medical University, Dr. Khanday leads the university’s strategic transformation in AI-driven medical education, overseeing the development and governance of AI-based education and research systems. Under her direction, DMU became the first medical university in the UAE to integrate GPT-powered agents within its Learning Management System and to integrate AI in curriculum reform .She has conceptualized and implemented several institutional initiatives, including the AI Xcelerate Hackathon, AI Integration in Curriculum and Research Writing Pilot, and E-Tuesdays Innovation Series, promoting AI literacy and innovation across the academic community. Her scholarly and leadership excellence earned her a nomination for the UNESCO King Hamad Bin Isa Al-Khalifa Prize for the Use of ICT in Education, recognizing her contributions to technology-enabled learning and equitable access to education. Dr. Khanday is the author of Quick Revision in Anatomy (CBS Publishers, 2014) and AI and I: Basics of Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Medical Education (2023). She has presented her research Nationally and continues to pioneer research at the intersection of healthcare, education, and emerging technologies.

Dr. Khanday has extensive teaching experience across undergraduate and postgraduate programs in medicine, nursing, and Pharmacy . Dr. Sami Mohamed
Assistant Professor – Internal Medicine

Dr. Sami Mohamed is an Assistant Professor and Consultant Internal Medicine with over a decade of experience in medical education, clinical practice, leadership, and scholarship. He earned his MRCP(UK) qualification from the Federation of the Royal Colleges of Physicians of the United Kingdom. He is a board certified Internal Medicine Consultant having completed his Clinical MD degree from Sudan Medical Specialization Board; and DHA licensed. He joined a Master of Health Professions Education program at SMSB, and later MSc program in Medical Education at University of Warwick, UK, and was elected to Fellowship of the Royal Colleges of Physicians of London, UK.

In addition to established faculty positions, he held roles in QAPE and EMREE Committees, participated in MRCP(UK) PACES exams organization, directed European Resuscitation Council (ERC) courses and trained Internal Medicine residents, interns and medical students; and presented in both local and international conferences.

Dr. Sami holds memberships in American College of Physicians, International Association for Health Professions Education (AMEE), American Diabetes Association, European Society of Cardiology, Emirates Medical Association, Emirates Society of Internal Medicine, and was accepted Fellow of International Diabetes Federation. At DMU, he works in Division of Internal Medicine, Department of Clinical Sciences, College of Medicine.

Dr. Nadia Mahmoud Mohamed Ali El Rouby is a distinguished Egyptian medical educator and histologist with an extensive academic and research background spanning more than three decades. She obtained her M.B.B.Ch. from Cairo University in 1985, followed by an M.Sc. (1990) and Ph.D. (1994) in Histology, and a Postgraduate Diploma in Pediatrics (1995). In 2017, she completed master’s in medical education (JMHPE) from Maastricht University, Netherlands, in collaboration with Suez Canal University, Egypt, ranking second in her class. Currently, she is working as Professor and Head of biomedical sciences Department at Dubai Medical University, College of Medicine. She also holds leadership roles such as Associate Dean of Student Affairs and Admissions and Head of Curriculum Review and Program Delivery Committees.

Her research contributions cover a wide range of histological and pathological studies, focusing on endocrine, hepatic, and reproductive systems, as well as innovative educational methodologies. Dr. El Rouby’s recent publications in international peer-reviewed journals underscore her ongoing commitment to biomedical science and education, particularly her interest in exploring natural remedies and drug safety at the cellular level.

Prof. Samia M. H. Farghaly
Professor & Head of Primary Health Care Division (Clinical Faculty)

Dr. Samia M. H. Farghaly is Professor and Head of the Primary Health Care Division at the College of Medicine and Specialist Senior Registrar at the Dubai Health Authority from 2004-2016 . With over five decades of distinguished service—spanning Bahrain (1978–2004) and the United Arab Emirates (2004–present)—she is recognized as a pioneer of Family Medicine education in the Gulf region and a leading advocate of the biopsychosocial model of care.

Her journey began in 1983 when she became the first Family Physician to qualify from Bahrain’s postgraduate Family Medicine Program, developed with the American University of Beirut. This landmark achievement preceded the establishment of the Arab Board of Family Medicine (1987) and was recognized as equivalent to consultant-level training. In 1992, she completed a Master’s in Psychiatry at Dublin University, strengthening her integration of psychological care within clinical practice.

During her 25-year tenure in Bahrain, Dr. Farghaly served as Consultant Family Physician and Maternal & Child Health Supervisor, leading antenatal, immunization, and family-planning services. She was also Faculty Tutor in the Postgraduate Family Medicine Residency Program and Undergraduate Instructor at the Arabian Gulf University, teaching clinical skills, communication, and patient-centered care. As an Examiner for the Arab Board, she contributed to OSCE design and assessment, training generations of family physicians across the region.

In Dubai, she practices family medicine in DHA 2 days/week and teaching family medicine residency program in Dubai for 3rd and 4th year resident preparing them for Arab board and participate in Arab board exam she helped establish the MRCGP [International] Examination, became Accredited Examiner (2005), and led the MCQ Module (2006–2012). At Dubai Medical College, she founded the Primary Health Care Division (2007), developed its curriculum, and created the Simulation Center.
Internationally, she remains an Accredited Examiner and Standard-Setting Panel Member for the MRCGP, advancing academic and clinical excellence globally.

Prof. Dr. Fahad Saqib Lodhi, PhD, MPH, MBBS, is a distinguished epidemiologist and public health leader with over 20 years of experience in clinical and community health. Currently serving as Professor and Chair of the Department of Public Health and Behavioral Sciences at Dubai Medical University, UAE (since August 2023), he drives innovative curricula, research, and community outreach focused on non-communicable diseases (NCDs), mental health, and health equity in conflict-affected regions. Previously, he held professorial roles at Women Medical and Dental College, Abbottabad, Pakistan (2020–2023), and contributed as a Public Health Specialist in Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Health (2016–2020), where he supervised postgraduate training and community interventions.

Dr. Lodhi’s PhD from Tehran University of Medical Sciences (2018) emphasized epidemiology and biostatistics, building on his MPH (2009) and MBBS (2004) from Pakistan. A prolific researcher, he has authored over 25 peer-reviewed publications, exploring quality of life, COVID-19 impacts, and psychosocial factors in vulnerable populations. His work integrates behavioral theories with data-driven advocacy, particularly for marginalized groups like refugees and low-SES communities. Committed to mentorship, he has supervised numerous theses and edited journals like the Journal of Women Medical & Dental College. Dr. Lodhi’s expertise bridges academia, policy, and practice, advancing NCD prevention in the MENA region.

Our Labs
Computational Research Laboratory

The Computational Research Laboratory provides a dedicated digital environment that supports all stages of the research process through specialized software and computational research tools. The laboratory offers access to applications for statistical analysis, data visualization, systematic reviews, scientific writing, reference management, grammar and language editing, graphical abstract and figure design. It supports undergraduate and postgraduate students, faculty, and researchers by enhancing research quality, productivity, and digital research competencies.
Drug Development Lab
Drug Development Laboratory

The Drug Development Laboratory supports teaching and research in the design, formulation, and evaluation of pharmaceutical products. It provides students and researchers with hands-on training in formulation development, preformulating studies, and quality assessment of dosage forms. The laboratory fosters innovation in pharmaceutical sciences by supporting faculty, undergraduate and postgraduate research aimed at developing safe, effective, and high-quality drug delivery systems.
Drug Discovery Labs
Drug Discovery labs

The Drug Discovery and Development Labs comprise two complementary sections: the Drug Discovery Lab and the Drug Development Lab. Together, they provide hands-on training in compound screening, purification, analytical investigation, characterization, pre-formulation, and formulation across a range of pharmaceutical products. Students develop practical skills and scientific reasoning that connect laboratory data with therapeutic potential, product quality, and overall performance.

Med AI Laboratory

The MedEd AI Research Lab at Dubai Medical University is an advanced innovation and research hub dedicated to transforming healthcare education through Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning (ML), Big Data analytics, and emerging digital technologies. The lab serves as a multidisciplinary platform where medical education, healthcare innovation, intelligent systems, wearable technologies, and digital transformation converge to shape the future of health professions education and healthcare delivery.

The lab focuses on the development, implementation, and evaluation of AI-powered educational ecosystems, including AI Virtual Tutors, AI Virtual Patients, adaptive learning systems, VR/AR-enabled classrooms, metaverse-based collaborative learning environments, and intelligent assessment platforms. It also supports cutting-edge research in machine learning models for healthcare prediction, big data-driven educational analytics, clinical decision support systems, predictive analytics, smart hospital technologies, interoperability in digital health, and precision medicine.

A major area of focus within the lab is the integration of Big Data and Machine Learning into healthcare education and research. The lab works on analyzing large-scale educational and healthcare datasets to identify learning patterns, improve student performance prediction, optimize curriculum delivery, support personalized learning pathways, and enhance clinical outcomes through data-driven insights. The research ecosystem also explores wearable health technologies, Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), biomedical data science, and AI-assisted diagnostics.

Through collaborations with healthcare institutions, universities, and technology partners, the MedEd AI Research Lab promotes innovation in teaching, learning, assessment, healthcare simulation, and translational research while ensuring ethical and responsible AI integration. The lab aims to position Dubai Medical University as a regional leader in AI-driven medical education, healthcare analytics, and future healthcare innovation by empowering faculty, students, researchers, and clinicians to design and deploy intelligent, future-ready healthcare and educational solutions.
Molecular Biology Laboratory

The Molecular Biology laboratory is dedicated for general molecular biology experiments, including reagent preparation, protein/DNA and RNA handling, and analysis using techniques such as Western Blotting and real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR).
Pharmacology Laboratory

The Pharmacology Laboratory supports teaching and research in drug discovery and development. It provides students and researchers with hands-on training in pharmacological techniques, including the study of drug mechanisms, efficacy, and safety using different experimental models. The laboratory is equipped to facilitate faculty, undergraduate and postgraduate research, fostering innovation and evidence-based pharmaceutical sciences.
Simulation Laboratory

The Simulation Lab is a purpose-built academic facility that supports competency-based, simulation-enhanced nursing education. The lab integrates high-, medium-, and low-fidelity simulation, immersive technologies, and authentic clinical equipment to ensure alignment with international standards in nursing education, patient safety, and quality of care.

Simulation-based learning is systematically embedded across the curriculum to develop clinical judgment, technical competence, communication, teamwork, and evidence-based practice within a safe and controlled learning environment.
Tissue Culture Lab
Tissue Culture Labs

The Tissue Culture Laboratory is a sterile laboratory for the growth, maintenance and testing of cancer cells and tissues under aseptic conditions. It enables controlled in-vitro studies, including cell growth analysis, drug testing, and molecular research related to cancer.

Apply

Lead

At DMU, sustainability is a core value that guides our operations, research, and community engagement — nurturing a greener future for Dubai and beyond.
Our Sustainability Strategic Direction
Inspiring a Healthier, More Sustainable Future

At Dubai Medical University, our sustainability strategic direction is to inspire and empower future generations to advance human health, environmental stewardship, and sustainable development through education, innovation, and responsible action. We are committed to embedding sustainability across education, research, campus operations, and community engagement by fostering environmental responsibility, social equity, and sustainable healthcare practices.

Through interdisciplinary learning, collaboration, and evidence-based action, DMU prepares healthcare professionals to contribute to healthier communities, more resilient systems, and a sustainable future, while advancing our role as a leading healthcare university committed to the well-being of people and the planet.
Our Sustainability Commitment

Through initiatives ranging from native Ghaf tree planting and plastic reduction to energy conservation and embracing sustainable construction practices, DMU is building a greener, more resilient campus that future generations will be proud to call their legacy.

Our sustainability strategy aligns with the UAE's Vision 2031 and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. We are committed to reducing our environmental footprint while simultaneously embedding sustainability literacy across our academic curricula in Medicine, Pharmacy, Nursing & Health-Science.

At Dubai Medical University, sustainability is embedded in our culture, guiding how we learn, lead, and serve. We believe that preparing future healthcare professionals requires more than academic excellence; it demands a commitment to environmental responsibility, social equity, and the long-term sustainability of the communities and ecosystems that underpin the health and well-being of current and future generations.

DMU Students Showcase Research and App Innovation at Khalifa University Longevity Conference

DMU Students Showcase Research and App Innovation at Khalifa University Longevity Conference Student from Dubai Medical University (DMU) presented an innovative project at the Longevity Conference hosted by Khalifa University,…

Student from Dubai Medical University (DMU) presented an innovative project at the Longevity Conference hosted by Khalifa University, demonstrating how student research can evolve into practical digital health solutions.

The project, titled “Colored Noise as a Non-Pharmacological Intervention for Sleep, Stress, and Healthy Aging: A Narrative Review,” was conducted by DMU studentNaba Hassan Hadi Almumareta and Aya Bchar Kanani from University of Sharjah under the supervision and original work on colored noise by Dr. Shifan Khanday Associate Dean of Research and Head of AI and Smart Education unit . The work explored how different forms of colored noise, including white, pink, and brown noise, may improve sleep quality, reduce stress levels, and support healthy aging.

During the conference presentation, the application was displayed on a tablet next to the research poster, allowing participants to experience how the scientific evidence could be translated into a practical digital wellness tool.

The project reflects Dubai Medical University’s emphasis on interdisciplinary student research and innovation, encouraging students to move beyond theoretical study and develop real-world digital health solutions. The collaboration with the University of Sharjah further highlights the value of cross-institutional partnerships in advancing student-led innovation in healthcare and longevity research.
